thread:
Paul (AE): Quick heads-up — FinEdge pilot starts Mon. Need SE help on Rust + Go SDK streaming handshake, tool/function-calls, and structured JSON output. Also need pricing confirmation and security Q answered. Who can take lead?
Sam (SE): I can take lead on the SDK side. Do they prefer SSE or websocket streaming? Any proxy/ingress in front?
Paul (AE): They said "existing edge proxy + authn via short-lived creds". Also asked about function-calling semantics for callbacks and whether structured output can map to their event schema.
Jia (SRE): For network: we'll need IP allowlist + ephemeral tokens if they keep their proxy. On Private, we can do VPC peering. If hosted, set up allowlist + TLS client certs.
Maria (Security): Heads-up — FinEdge has a SOC2 + FedRAMP-ish checklist. They'll request SAML SSO + SCIM for users, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs retention. I need the security questionnaire filled before pilot access. Link to our template: https://redwood.internal/security/questionnaire/FE123
Alex (Sales Eng): Pricing note — pilot usage can be covered by an initial credit allocation. For dedicated resources we may need a short-term reserved commit if sustained throughput required. I'll confirm numbers after we scope expected tokens/qps.
Sam (SE): For the SDKs, quick notes: Rust client supports streaming over websockets today; Go client has SSE support but missing small piece for structured toolcall events (we have a PR in review). Workaround: stream raw chunks and post-process into toolcall frames on the client.
Sam (SE): Example handshake (can paste into their devs):
```
POST /v1/handshake HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "protocol": "websocket", "capabilities": ["streaming","tool-calls","structured-output"], "model": "redwood-serve-v1" }
```
Sam (SE): And an example structured output payload we emit for a function call:
```
{"choices":[{"content":{"type":"structured","value":{"action":"create_refund","params":{"order_id":"ABC123","amount":120.00}}}}]}
```
Paul (AE): Nice. Can we guarantee ordering for streamed tool-call chunks? FinEdge will apply events in order.
Jia (SRE): We provide sequence numbers in the stream and a small buffered reorder window. For very low-latency strict ordering we can pin to a single producer thread (affects throughput). I'll share the perf tradeoffs in the runbook.
Maria (Security): For security questionnaire items we need: 1) encryption at rest & in transit 2) KMS/HSM design 3) access review cadence 4) incident response SLA. I'll start drafting answers; need input from infra on KMS.
Alex (Sales Eng): Also FYI: tool/function calling in pilot — we should discuss fallback policy if the tool fails (retry vs. NACK). Customers often want idempotency keys.
Sam (SE): We recommend idempotency keys and safe retries. For the SDKs we expose an auto-retry helper that includes a client-provided idempotency token.
Paul (AE): Blockers checklist from FinEdge: (a) security questionnaire, (b) short-lived creds workflow, (c) confirm streaming protocol, (d) pilot pricing/credit.
Sam (SE): I'll open a small repo with example Rust + Go snippets and a sandbox handshake script by EOD today.
Jia (SRE): I'll add a note in the runbook about IP allowlist + ephemeral token TTLs and the canary fallback to a smaller instance if capacity spikes.
Maria (Security): I'll start the questionnaire and ping Legal for the NDA + any compliance addenda.
Paul (AE): Great — can we sync tomorrow 10am PT for a 30m run-through with FinEdge devs? If yes, I'll send invite and include the repo + questionnaire draft. :calendar:
Alex (Sales Eng): 10am works for me.
Sam (SE): Works. I'll bring the SDK snippets. :thumbsup:
Jia (SRE): OK for me.
Maria (Security): Sounds good — I'll join and present the sec items.
bridge-bot: Meeting created: FinEdge pilot runbook sync — Tue 10:00 PT. Link: https://meet.redwood/finedge-pilot
Paul (AE): Thanks all — I'll attach the questionnaire and the initial scope doc in the invite. (reacts :eyes:)
